feedback: Approve for this race. The candidate tests one hypothesis from iteration 2 (the 0.08 m sensor span is the cause of line loss) and one damping change (kd 0.3 to 0.45). The evidence supports the geometry hypothesis. In iteration 2 line_loss_events stayed at 1.0 to 1.05 in all 60 trials, and max_error sat at 0.062 to 0.064 across iterations 0 to 2. That is just past the 0.06 m off-track limit, and it matches the point where the outermost sensor reads no tape. Iteration 2 also showed steering_oscillation of 0.30 on the oval and 0.28 on the s-bend at kp 3.0, kd 0.3, so raising kd is a reasonable response. The candidate is valid: all sensor x values sit within ±0.08 m, sensor_size 0.016 is allowed, and the weights, line_loss and observation list are all allowed. Nothing is obviously broken. The weak point is that two changes race together, so the result will not isolate which one helped. That is a cost I accept, because the iteration budget is limited and the two symptoms are separate. Completion within 3 s is unlikely at base_speed 1.2, so progress and line-loss telemetry are the useful outputs. This is early exploration with 8 iterations left, so racing now is worth more than another reading-only round. I cannot say how it will perform. Next race, read the results as follows. If line_loss_events is still about 1.0 with the wider span, sensor span is probably not the cause. Test sensor y position (move the row closer to or further from the axle) or sensor_size 0.012 next. If line_loss_events falls well below 1.0 but steering_oscillation is still above 0.2 at kd 0.45, lower kp toward 2.6 before changing speed. If the run is clean (line_loss_events near 0, steering_oscillation under 0.2, max_error under 0.06), raise base_speed in 0.1 steps to 1.3, then 1.4, to test completion_time under 3 s.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays near 1.0 with the ±0.07 m span, keep base_speed 1.2 and test sensor y position or sensor_size 0.012 (iteration 2 showed line loss at 1.0 across all tracks at span ±0.04, so span alone may not be the cause).

If line_loss_events drops but steering_oscillation stays above 0.2 with kd 0.45, lower kp from 3.0 toward 2.6 and keep kd at 0.45 (iteration 2 at kp 3.0, kd 0.3 gave oscillation of 0.30 on the oval and 0.28 on the s-bend).

If the run is clean (line_loss_events near 0, steering_oscillation under 0.2, max_error under 0.06), raise base_speed in 0.1 steps to 1.3, then 1.4, keeping kp and kd fixed, to test completion_time under 3 s (iteration 1 reached progress 0.37 on the oval at base_speed 1.4, so the speed limit is not yet known).
